articles.body: James Bond may never miss, but Robert Pattinson's casting as the next iconic British secret agent was positively shocking to fans across the world. Pattinson, 40, called the role "the honor of a lifetime," in a statement released Monday where "Dune" director Denis Villeneuve was also tapped to bring Bond back to the big screen following Daniel Craig's 15-year reign as 007. Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo admitted he was "shaken, not stirred" by the casting choice. ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND "As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for," Arroyo told Fox News Digital. "After five Bond films with Daniel Craig in the lead, it was probably time to bring back some of the fun and charm that Pierce Brosnan and Roger Moore brought to the franchise." He noted how Pattinson was known for his "brooding and dark qualities," a contrast to the more masculine qualities a Bond character usually brings to the screen. FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION "As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for." "Fun and a light touch is not the first thing that comes to mind when you think of his filmography," Arroyo said. "His Batman was a pretty dreary affair, the sequel of which I could care less about seeing. Bond also requires a certain physicality and strength – he is an assassin after all." Arroyo believed Henry Cavill "would have been a much better choice all round." "But it sounds like MGM/Amazon wants to give audiences a darker, moodier Bond – just when the public is craving a good, old-fashioned escape. articles.title: Sharad Kapoor alleges people filmed donation videos and took the money back: 'Haath mein paise diya, pata hi nahi chal raha hai kaun kya kar raha hai'
articles.summary: Sharad Kapoor, who recently sought financial help and work amid his failing health, has now complained that some people are using his situation to create
articles.body: Sharad Kapoor, who recently sought financial help and work amid his failing health, has now complained that some people are using his situation to create social media content. In a video posted on Tuesday, November 17, he claimed that visitors handed him money, recorded the moment and then took the cash back. Upset by this, he said he will no longer meet anyone.His friend Hema Choudhary of Bezubaan Trust has also requested the public to stop approaching him for videos and donation reels. Hema, who first brought his condition into the public eye, said that he needs medical treatment and peace, not repeated demands for bytes. The trust has also cautioned people about fake fundraising accounts using his name.Sharad Kapoor says money was taken back after videos were shotIn his new video, Sharad Kapoor first thanked the film industry, his fans and everyone who reached out after hearing about his plight. At the same time, he said he felt uneasy about the misleading clips doing the rounds online.Sharad said, "I would like the film industry, my fans, and the people who really care about me. I’m so thankful to you. Aap logon ne itna pyaar diya hai aap soch bhi nahi sakte. Lekin social media pe bahot saari galat chize dikhaye jaa rahi hai… haath mein paise diya… pata hi nahi chal raha hai kaun kya kar raha hai. Samaj hi nahi aa raha hai."According to the actor, some visitors pushed notes into his hands without asking him, shot the exchange on camera and later collected the money again. Following these experiences, he indicated that he does not wish to receive visitors anymore.Hema Choudhary urges people to stop filming the actorHema Choudhary said she had been hesitant to speak openly about Sharad Kapoor’s condition because he is physically frail. Her aim, she explained, was to arrange help, especially medical aid, and not to push him into the glare of publicity.She said, "Main chaah rahi thi public mein zyada expose naa ho Sharad ki condition kyuki unki tabiyat kharab hai. Vo kya baat karte hai unko nahi pata hai. Uss din maine appeal ki help ki, logon ne mujhe hi troll kiya. Maine animals ke liye video daala ki animals ko help mile, vo sab bure haal mein the (I wanted to ensure that Sharad's condition was not overly exposed in public because he is unwell. He doesn't even realise what he is saying. That day, I appealed for help, but people ended up trolling me instead. I also posted a video requesting people to help the animals, as they were all in a terrible condition)."She added, "I represent animal welfare. Aap Sharad Kapoor ke bure haalat ka tamasha kar rahe ho. He is in trauma, he’s not stable. Aap aa kar zabardasti unki byte le rahi ho. Do not disturb him, do not harass him. Humne aap se paise nahi maange. Usko medical attention ki zaroorat hai, jo hum arrange kar rahe hai (I represent animal welfare. You are turning Sharad Kapoor's deteriorating condition into a spectacle. He is traumatised and not in a stable state of mind. You are approaching him and forcibly trying to get a byte from him. Please do not disturb or harass him. We have not asked you for any money. He needs medical attention, which we are currently arranging)."She also revealed that she asked Sharad why he had taken money from a person he did not seem to know. He reportedly told her that the stranger had pushed the cash on him, recorded the scene and then taken it back.Posting the video, she wrote, “Please please leave him also for his life… stop making donation reels.”Welfare trust cautions against fake accountsAs donation-themed content spread online, Bezubaan Trust put out a separate note on Instagram. It told the public to stay away from any page claiming to raise funds for Sharad or for the organisation.“We are not associated with any of the Sharad Kapoor’s accounts…all are fake. Do not believe or donate if anyone appeals for donation,” the statement read.This alert came after Sharad Kapoor’s recent clips drew a wave of people wanting to help him.How Sharad Kapoor’s health troubles became publicWorries about the actor began when a video of him in tears went viral. He was upset because his four pet dogs had been moved to an animal welfare centre due to his health condition.A later clip posted welfare trust showed him speaking about his battle with depression. In it, he also requested the film fraternity for financial support and acting work.Sharad Kapoor’s film careerSharad Kapoor began his Bollywood journey with ‘Mera Pyara Bharat’ and became better known through ‘Dastak’ (1996), the film that also marked Sushmita Sen’s entry into Hindi cinema.His other works include ‘Tamanna’, ‘Josh’, ‘Khauff’, ‘Kyo Kii… Main Jhuth Nahin Bolta’, ‘Jaani Dushman: Ek Anokhi Kahani’, ‘LOC Kargil’ and ‘Lakshya’. articles.title: Archana Puran Singh’s son Aayushmaan reveals how parents reacted to his six-year age gap with fiancée Samiksha: ‘What if he is not ready to be serious?’
articles.summary: Archana Puran Singh and Parmeet Sethi’s younger son, Aayushmaan Sethi, recently took his relationship with girlfriend Samiksha Shetty to the next level by
articles.body: Archana Puran Singh and Parmeet Sethi’s younger son, Aayushmaan Sethi, recently took his relationship with girlfriend Samiksha Shetty to the next level by proposing to her during their holiday in Italy. Samiksha had moved into the Sethi family’s Madh Island home earlier this year, and following their engagement, curiosity around the couple’s wedding plans has been growing. In a new vlog on his YouTube channel, Aayushmaan and Samiksha addressed several questions from fans, offering an update on their wedding preparations, finances and decision to live together before marriage.One of the first things fans wanted to know was when the couple planned to tie the knot. Aayushmaan revealed that wedding discussions have already become a regular topic at home. “This is a huge discussion in our house right now,” he shared, prompting Samiksha to add, “Every day.” He further explained that their families are in the process of matching their horoscopes, while a formal meeting between the Sethi and Shetty families is still awaited. “Our horoscopes are being matched right now, and they are yet to match them. There is still a big family meeting coming,” he said.Although a wedding date has not been decided, Aayushmaan indicated that the couple does not intend to prolong the wait. “We have no idea (about the date) yet but it will be approximately in a year or a year and a half. We won’t wait too long,” he said. The couple is yet to work out details such as the venue and other arrangements. Admitting that the process already feels overwhelming, he added, “Wedding planning is very stressful. Weddings are too expensive. It hasn’t even started yet and we are already stressed. We don’t know how we will do it but we will do it together,” he said.The vlog also touched upon the six-year age difference between the couple, with Samiksha being older than Aayushmaan. Asked how their respective families responded to their age gap, she revealed that the initial concern was whether Aayushmaan was ready for a serious relationship. “They were just concerned because they were thinking, ‘What if he is not ready to be serious?’. Very early on we realised that this was not the case so it was sorted then. They were quite happy. He is the poster child of a good boy. They are very happy when he visits.”Aayushmaan, meanwhile, pointed out that the age difference was not a major concern for his parents, Archana and Parmeet, as they themselves have a seven-year age gap.The couple also spoke about how they manage their money. Responding to a question about their finances, Aayushmaan said, “Our finances are separate so far. Eventually, we will combine them.” Samiksha explained that they currently handle their individual expenses independently, with him paying for his requirements and her managing hers. A yoga instructor by profession, Samiksha is also a social media influencer, while Aayushmaan primarily works as a YouTuber and content creator.He also offered a glimpse into how expenses are shared at the Sethi household, particularly when it comes to groceries. Rather than maintaining a fixed arrangement, different family members contribute whenever required. “We share that in the household. Sometimes I give it, sometimes my parents, sometimes Samiksha. It’s a mix. No one is keeping a tab of the groceries. Our main expenditure is travel, and we split that 50/50,” he shared.Another topic that came up was their decision to move in together before getting married. Aayushmaan said the arrangement has worked well for them and believes living together can help couples understand each other better before taking the next step. “It is good for us. I think if you can live together before marriage, you will find if you are right for each other or not,” he said.Samiksha added that sharing a home also gives couples an opportunity to understand their partner’s family dynamics, temperament and anger issues. Aayushmaan further noted that everyday habits, including eating and sleeping patterns, can also become apparent when two people live together. “Some things become a problem in the future if you know now, you can actually grow together,” he said.Samiksha also spoke about the contrast between their family backgrounds and how living together has helped them navigate those differences. “The two of us come from very different families. My family is quite soft-spoken, shy, conservative. His family is full-on entertainment, loud, Punjabi, funny, very different.”Aayushmaan and Samiksha have been dating for over a year and began living together in May 2026. articles.body: Robert Pattinson’s casting as the new James Bond has taken many fans by surprise, but Brad Pitt is fully on board. articles.body: Lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar recently looked back on an encounter with India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, which took place on the latter's birthday in 1963. articles.summary: This November, four prominent artists bring alive countless stories on canvas An at gallery is showcasing the works of four leading artists in Chandigarh.
articles.body: This November, four prominent artists bring alive countless stories on canvasAn at gallery is showcasing the works of four leading artists in Chandigarh. City based Pardeep Singh and Gaurvi Sharma and Hyderabad based Bolgum Sai Aditya and Manas Bholla form the four square, the ‘Chaturth’, in this showcase of four distinct artistic voices, each offering a unique way of seeing, interpreting, and engaging with the world.“The exhibition of a creative confluence of these four artists and we couldn’t think of a more apt title than Chaturth. articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1' continues to enjoy a phenomenal run at the box office, having crossed the Rs 1,400 crore mark worldwide and Rs 750 crore in India. Amid the film's impressive performance, questions have been raised about whether the two-part saga, backed by Namit Malhotra and reportedly mounted on a staggering Rs 4,000 crore budget, will be able to recover its massive investment. Actor Lara Dutta, who plays Queen Kaikeyi in the film, has now shared her thoughts on the possibility of achieving that milestone.In an exclusive conversation with NDTV, Lara expressed confidence that the film would not only recover its costs but also surpass expectations. She said, "We're finally standing, literally, as giants alongside the best of the best films that have been made anywhere else in the world. And it takes so much internal strength to drown out the naysayers and the doubters, and then just keep focused on your vision and keep going. So, will the film make its money back or recover it? I am pretty, pretty, pretty certain it will, not just through the box office, but with whatever Namit has decided to do with it. I don't think it will just recover. I think it will far surpass it."The actor also praised the scale of the ambitious project and Malhotra's conviction in bringing it to life. Speaking about the pride she felt watching the film at its premiere, she added, "I say it is tremendous. It takes a tremendous amount of bravery to put your money where your mouth is, literally, and to create something like this. articles.title: David Beckham sues after his fragrance is sold in gas stations and discount stores
articles.summary: A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.
articles.body: LONDON — A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon. Beckham’s commercial company is suing a beauty firm after his “luxury” fragrances were allegedly found for sale in discount stores and a gas station bargain bin. DB Ventures has filed a claim in the New York Supreme Court against German beauty group Coty, which makes and distributes a range of Beckham-branded fragrances and toiletries. They include the Classic and Instinct lines and the eaux de toilette Intimately and Exquisite Leather. The claim argues that Beckham’s “world-renowned global brand is synonymous with excellence and refinement,” and “David Beckham products are a symbol of everyday luxury.” “Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station,” the legal document says. “How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed.” Lawyers for DB Ventures allege that Beckham-branded products “ended up in the bargain bin inside a gas station” and at British budget retailer Poundland, “allowing the product to be sold for dollar store prices and associating the David Beckham brand with cheap, discount products.” DB Ventures is seeking at least $41 million in damages for breach of its licensing agreement. Coty has asked a judge to dismiss the lawsuit, which was filed in April. The company argues that New York courts have no jurisdiction in the case, and says DB Ventures is using the claim to “manufacture its early exit” from its licensing deal and hand over the Beckham contracts to another firm, Interparfums. Coty and DB Ventures did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. Beckham, the former soccer star for Manchester United and Real Madrid and captain of the England men’s national team, parlayed success on the pitch into a lucrative business career that includes co-ownership of soccer team Inter Miami. He was knighted last year by King Charles III, becoming Sir David. He also has had a very public persona as a fashion model, “Bend it Like Beckham” movie muse and is husband to Spice Girl-turned-fashion designer Victoria “Posh Spice” Beckham. The couple have four children. The Sunday Times Rich list earlier this year estimated the Beckhams’ wealth at almost 1.2 billion pounds ($1.58 billion).

articles.title: Nature Photographer of the Year 2026 reveals exceptional images from our wild world
articles.summary: Finnish photographer Hannu Ahonen has been named Nature Photographer of the Year 2026 for an image of a water lily leaf next to a carbon copy made of ice.
articles.body: Finnish photographer Hannu Ahonen has been named Nature Photographer of the Year 2026 for an image of a water lily leaf next to a carbon copy made of ice. Ahonen’s photograph, named “The One that Left and the One that Stayed,” beat more than 27,000 entries from photographers from 96 countries, according the Nature Talks Photo Festival, which organizes the competition. The organizers also named a number of category winners, including an image of a giraffe’s head peeking out of some mist, and a drone shot of peach blossoms in the snow. “It is not often that a photograph of a plant is crowned the overall winner of a major photography competition, but the jury could not overlook this fascinating image by Hannu Ahonen,” said Theo Bosboom, chair of the judging panel, in a statement published Saturday. “First and foremost, the photograph captures a unique situation: a water lily leaf with an almost perfect black-and-white replica of it lying next to it in the water,” he said. “It takes a moment for the viewer to realise what has happened here: a thin layer of ice that had formed on the leaf has been blown away by the wind,” added Bosboom. “The shapes in the sheet of ice are delicate; even the veins of the water lily leaf are clearly recognisable.” Ahonen said that he took the photo at a time when the winter ice had arrived, but snow hadn’t fallen. “Some of the pond’s lily pad leaves began to crumble on top of the ice,” he said in the statement. “The wind carried a few of them away, revealing delicate, frosty ornaments left behind,” he added. “I eagerly captured this natural phenomenon, something I had never witnessed before.” Other photos honored by the organizers include a picture of a Malayan sun bear sleeping inside a garbage incinerator, and an underwater view of a polar bear peering into a hole in the ice sheet. Entries for next year’s competition open on November 20.

articles.summary: Bradley Whitford claimed on ABC's "The View" that 60,000 people are held in "internment camps," referencing ICE detention under the Trump administration.
articles.body: "West Wing" actor Bradley Whitford claimed that there are 60,000 people currently locked in "internment camps" in the U.S. during a Monday appearance on ABC's "The View." During his appearance on the panel, Whitford said he was relieved by the election results, which he described as relegating an "authoritarian, cruel impulse" to the "ash heap of history." However, he said he still had concerns. "I was looking today that...we have internment camps," Whitford said. "There are 60,000 people in internment camps. MADDOW FEARS TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS MAY BE USED TO IMPRISON ‘THE REST OF US’ "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin agreed with Whitford, saying, "Yeah, we do." Whitford appeared to be referring to reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) was holding approximately 60,000 people in detention centers as part of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. "Comparing ICE detention centers to World War II internment camps is disgusting," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. "No lawbreakers in human history have been better treated than illegal aliens in the U.S. These types of smears by Hollywood elites and the media are leading to our ICE law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,600% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, terrorists, and gang members," she added. In his comments on "The View," Whitford did not directly compare ICE detention centers to World War II internment camps. articles.title: Ray Tintori, filmmaker and boyfriend of ‘SNL’ alum Heidi Gardner, dies at 43
articles.summary: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday.
articles.body: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday. Tintori was 43 and the agency did not divulge to exact date of death or the cause of death. “We are investigating and the cause and manner of death are pending further study,” a spokesperson for the agency said in an email to NBC News. There was no immediate comment from Gardner, who left “SNL” in August 2025 after eight seasons with the show. But pinned to the top of Tintori’s Instagram page was a July 27, 2025 post in which he wrote “Happy birthday to the angel of reality @heidilgardner.” Gardner was born July 27, 1983. “Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes.” Tintori also called her the “sexiest woman who ever lived.” “The world is a love letter to you,” he wrote in closing. “I am your boy forever.” The son of film editor John Tintori and the late script supervisor Mary Cybulski, Tintori is best known for the psychedelic music videos he directed for the indie bands MGMT and Arcade Fire. In addition, Tintori directed videos for musical acts such as Chairlift, Bonnie Prince Billy, The Cool Kids, The Killers and Solange. Tintori was also a founding member of Court 13, the filmmaking collective behind the movie “Beasts of the Southern Wild.” He was the special effects unit director on the 2012 film, which was nominated for four Oscars. In 2017, Tintori won a Sports Emmy for co-directing “Follow My Lead: The Story of the 2016 NBA Finals,” a 360-degree virtual reality documentary. Most recently, Tintori in 2025 co-directed a performance of Ethan Coen’s one-act play “Waiting.” Tintori also had a cameo as a newsreel photographer in the 2025 movie “Marty Supreme.”

The Emmy-winning 'Delhi Crime' filmmaker Richie Mehta's will direct the five-part series version. The shooting of the show will take place in India.'A Passage to India' plotAccording to Variety, the series will be set in the 1920s and follows Aziz (Fazal), a local doctor who has spent years caring for others and who sets out to convince his Indian friends that real friendship with the British can survive colonial rule. His hopes start to come apart after an unexplained episode at the Marabar Caves, which leaves him accused of assault.The scandal stirs up violent feelings and builds to a trial that grips the public. articles.title: Ranking the top five James Bond movies in honor of Robert Pattinson becoming the new 007
articles.summary: With Robert Pattinson cast as 007, here's a ranking of the best James Bond films, from "Goldeneye" and "Goldfinger" to "Casino Royale" and Timothy Dalton.
articles.body: You've all heard the news already, but if you haven't, Robert Pattinson has been tapped to play 007 in the newest installment of the James Bond franchise. I've seen plenty of back and forth about whether this was the right move, but I urge everyone to reserve judgment until actually seeing the movie. People freaked out when "the vampire from those 'Twilight' movies" donned the cape and cowl to play Batman, and I'd say he did a fine job. ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND James Bond fans are quietly some of the most opinionated and psychotic fans there are; I'd put them up there with Star Wars fans, though they're less terminally online than their sci-fi counterparts. With all that said, I thought I'd poke the hornet's nest a bit and give you all my top five favorite James Bond films. I'll be pulling from the 25 officially recognized 007 movies and ranking them based on how entertaining they are, how good the actor in question does playing Bond, the gadgets, the girls, the quotes, you name it. I'll even throw the Bond themes in for good measure. Without any further ado, let's piss off some fanboys! Honorable Mention: "The Living Daylights," "Thunderball," "Dr. No," "A View to a Kill," "The World Is Not Enough" 5. "Tomorrow Never Dies" (1997) Though many believe Pierce Brosnan's first turn as Bond was his best (more on that in a bit), it's his second outing that often gets overlooked. Alas, "Tomorrow Never Dies" lacks some of the flash and sizzle of its immediate predecessor, but it's perhaps a more realistic plot (and prescient, too). Jonathan Pryce plays Elliot Carver, a media mogul hellbent on starting a war between China and the UK, and does so with such aplomb, walking the line between scene-chewing psychopath and genuinely believable real-world villain. FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION Carver uses his media company and 24-hour news cycle stranglehold to manipulate headlines with the goal of starting an armed conflict between two global superpowers. Brosnan as Bond is probably at his most comfortable in this movie, settling into the role and firing off quips like a seasoned veteran. The gadgets in this one are a perfect blend of fun, spy movie toys and practical tools, and I especially love the remote-controlled BMW. Special mention has to go to Michelle Yeoh as Chinese intelligence operative Wai Lin. She's perhaps the first Bond girl that truly feels like an equal counterpart to 007, and their action set pieces together are outstanding. For the title track, Sheryl Crow brings it, and it happens to be one of my favorite Bond themes; timeless yet perfect for the 90s'90s-era 007 films all the same. This movie often gets lost in the shuffle, but "Tomorrow Never Dies" deserves to be counted among the best in the series. 4. "Casino Royale" (2006) Alright, I have to get this out of the way now: I loathe Daniel Craig as James Bond. To me, his turn as the supposedly super suave secret agent always felt more like "Jason Bourne in a tux," although it made sense for the series to turn this direction after the bloated monstrosity that was 2002's "Die Another Day." With all that said, I still have to give Craig his flowers for "Casino Royale," which was essentially a gritty reboot of the entire franchise. It's treated as a prequel and origin story, and shows Bond as both vulnerable and green around the gills. Mads Mikkelsen as Le Chiffre is great, and at times he carries the film all by itself (sometimes you're only as good as your Bond villain). It takes itself a little too seriously at times, but as I mentioned before, this felt like the next logical step after letting things get a little too silly. Bond films are often responses to the cultural zeitgeist (see "Moonraker"), so 007 becoming a gruff action star worked in 2006. The gadgets are no frills, the fight sequences are brutally realistic, and Craig brings the physicality in droves. Even if you're a Bond traditionalist like I am, this one is worth a watch. 3. "License To Kill" (1989) Anyone who thought Daniel Craig was the first gritty, emotionally tormented Bond must have just started following the series in the 90s, because before Craig there was Timothy Dalton. Dalton only had two films as 007, but he only needed two films to leave a lasting legacy as everyone's favorite secret agent. His first film, "The Living Daylights," is a personal favorite of mine, and features a tailor-made, late 80s Cold War plotline. "License To Kill" scraps all of that for a grounded revenge plot, with Bond turning his back on MI6 and his country to track down the drug kingpin who killed his best friend and coworker. The sets are exotic, and the action is intense for an 80s spy movie, and Dalton gives us the most brutal interpretation of Bond up to that point while still being charming and debonair enough to pass for a lady-killing 00-agent. While Dalton is the shining star thanks to the emotional weight he brings to the role, Robert Davi crushes it as Franz Sanchez, the psychopathic drug lord and main antagonist. Benicio del Toro also does a phenomenal job as Dario, Sanchez's right-hand man, and Carey Lowell deserves special mention as well. Her role as Pam Bouvier was the blueprint for more capable Bond girls like Wai Lin who followed in her footsteps. Finally, the title track is outstanding, and probably my personal favorite. Gladys Knight puts her whole body into belting out the movie's theme, and she does a great job of bringing a more "modern" feel to the Shirley Bassey template from earlier movies. Give this one a watch, then remember that Timothy Dalton owns Daniel Craig. 2. "Goldfinger" (1964) If you're looking for the quintessential Bond movie, the one which all others would follow for years to come, it's "Goldfinger." This is the birthplace of pretty much every trope that would be featured in 007 films, even today. The over-the-top gadgets, the Bond girls, the dastardly villain and memorable henchmen, the exotic locales, it's all here. Sean Connery absolutely kills it as 007, and this is probably where the theory that every actor does his best job in his third Bond film. It almost feels like Connery peaked in "Goldfinger," with everything from his look to his line delivery being so perfect. There are so many memorable lines, so many classic set pieces, an unforgettable bad guy; I can't say enough great things about this movie. "Goldfinger" is so ubiquitous that it's even the genesis for the third Austin Powers film, "Goldmember." When your movie is so ingrained in pop culture that it even spawns a successful parody of the source material, you know you've made it. 1. "Goldeneye" (1995) I know I said "Goldfinger" was the quintessential Bond movie, but for my money, the best overall 007 film has to be "Goldeneye." Maybe that's just the 90s kid in me, but I don't care. It's Pierce Brosnan's first try as the famous spy, and many believe it is his finest hour. Much like Daniel Craig after him, Brosnan's spin as Bond was seen as a rebirth of sorts for the series, though there are still hints of Cold War spy themes throughout. Bond has to battle the former USSR as well as a friend-turned-foe in Alec Trevelyan (played brilliantly by Sean Bean), and it's that added bit of betrayal that puts this movie over the top. Both Bond girls are fantastic in this one, and Famke Janssen's role as the psycho Xenia Onatopp (clever name) is instantly memorable. All of that is great, but Brosnan is the star of this one and it's not close. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's almost like the man was built in a lab to play James Bond, and "Goldeneye" is him at his absolute "Bond-iest." He's the perfect blend of suave and sophisticated while still having his goofy moments, almost making him feel a little more human than he did in some of his later roles. Timothy Dalton is my personal favorite Bond, but Brosnan is who my mind conjures up if I ever think about the character. Oh, and Tina Turner's contribution to the movie's title track is fantastic. A true banger if there ever was one. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If I needed to show someone a single 007 movie to get them hooked on the franchise, "Goldeneye" is the choice every time.

articles.summary: Bezos said that he and director Denis Villeneuve were immediately drawn to Robert Pattinson’s performance during screen tests.
articles.body: Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who’s making the franchise’s next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too. During Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was “heavily involved” in the process of casting the newest 007: > We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was really interesting — full costume, real sets, other actors. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screening tests, and reviewing all of that. And all of the actors were extraordinarily talented. > By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. It was kind of immediately undebated. Denis — the director — we all sort of gravitated to Rob. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him, just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, ‘maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.’ But in the screen test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond. [Media: It’s not exactly surprising that a studio leader would want to have a say in casting the new face for one of their most lucrative franchises. But with Bezos being so hands-on, one can only image what this new era of Bond films will look and feel like once Amazon starts releasing them in theaters.

articles.title: 81-year-old former teacher goes viral after dancing with Chris Brown at L.A. concert
articles.summary: A viral moment from Chris Brown’s Los Angeles concert Sunday with Usher has made Joyce Lakin an unexpected internet sensation.
articles.body: A viral moment from Chris Brown’s Los Angeles concert Sunday with Usher has made Joyce Lakin an unexpected internet sensation. The 81-year-old former teacher from West Hollywood was brought on stage at SoFi Stadium during Brown’s “Take You Down” performance, which is a portion of the show where the singer seductively dances on a female fan. Sunday’s interaction began with Brown on a pole serenading Lakin, who was carrying a red cane and dressed in a long zebra-print fur coat, a furry hat and sunglasses. The crowd erupted in cheers as Lakin danced with the singer. Lakin was then moved to a nearby red couch where the steamy performance continued. “I didn’t have time to really freak out,” Lakin said by phone Tuesday. “I just said, ‘I’m going to go with it.’” Lakin said she asked her youngest daughter to take her to Brown and Usher’s “R&B Tour” after Lakin was diagnosed with cancer this summer. She said she underwent surgery in August to remove a tumor from her intestines. “She wanted something to look forward to,” her daughter, Lori Lakin Hutcherson, said. “I couldn’t say no.” Lakin said she bought her fur coat, hat and purse, knowing that her look “would create some kind of attention.” But she never expected to be called onto the stage. She said she was initially approached by a woman she believes is a dancer for Brown. The woman complimented her outfit and dance moves, Lakin said. Two men later approached and asked Lakin if she wanted to go on stage, she said. “I said, ‘Of course.’ And they said, ‘Take my hand,’” she recalled. Lakin said she has always loved music and dancing and was not nervous about being in the spotlight. “The music helps you go; you keep the beat. And I love music. It’s always been a part of my life, and dancing as well,” she said. “So, I got on there, and I said, ‘I can’t just stand here.’” Lakin Hutcherson had no idea her mother would be called on stage. Lakin Hutcherson was seated a few rows ahead of her mother, who was in an accessible section. “I’m watching the show, and the next thing I know, my mother is on stage. And I’m just as shocked and open-mouthed as anybody,” she said. After the performance, the mother and daughter said they were escorted by a member of the crew to a VIP section to take in the rest of the show. Lakin said she also got to meet Tank, Mario and Bobby Brown backstage. Lakin said she never expected videos of her to go viral but wants to encourage people “to believe in themselves and live their best life to the fullest.” “I had the time of my life,” she said. “It was truly unforgettable in every way.”

articles.title: Variety recommends trans actress Hunter Schafer as next Bond girl alongside Robert Pattinson
articles.summary: Variety recommended trans "Euphoria" star Hunter Schafer as the next Bond girl opposite new 007 Robert Pattinson, saying the casting would "make history."
articles.body: Variety recommended transgender actress Hunter Schafer as a potential Bond girl opposite Robert Pattinson in the upcoming James Bond film on Monday, suggesting the casting could "make history." After the "Twilight" series and "The Batman" star was announced as the latest actor to take over the role of 007, Variety published a list of 19 actresses who could play his love interest. The list included established Hollywood stars such as Emily Blunt and Margot Robbie, along with newer faces such as "One Battle After Another" actress Chase Infiniti and "Obsession" star Inde Navarrette. Schafer was the only transgender actor on the list, and Variety's writers highlighted her as a potential standout. ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND "Not only would Hunter Schafer make history as the first trans Bond girl, she’d be a damn good one," the article read. The magazine pointed to Schafer's experience in the HBO series "Euphoria" and her role in the upcoming Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099" as evidence of her acting credentials and potential chemistry with Pattinson. "We could totally see Schafer and Pattinson sharing flirty banter before going head-to-head against some baddies — and just imagine the looks on that press tour!" Variety added. IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE Fox News Digital reached out to Amazon MGM Studios for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Pattinson's casting followed years of anticipation after Daniel Craig's appearance as Bond in 2021's "No Time to Die." During that period, commentators proposed casting an actor of color or a woman as 007. The announcement of Pattinson's casting, surprised longtime franchise fans, including Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo. "As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for," Arroyo told Fox News Digital. "After five Bond films with Daniel Craig in the lead, it was probably time to bring back some of the fun and charm that Pierce Brosnan and Roger Moore brought to the franchise. "But it sounds like MGM/Amazon wants to give audiences a darker, moodier Bond — just when the public is craving a good, old-fashioned escape," he added. "We’ll see if audiences wish this new Bond to ‘Live or Let Die.’" FORMER JAMES BOND ACTRESS PANS AMAZON FRANCHISE TAKEOVER AS 'ABSOLUTE MADNESS' In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Media Research Center's Newsbusters executive editor Tim Graham described the article as a result of woke journalism interacting with classic Hollywood. "We know what happened when they tried to make the ‘Ghostbusters’ an all-girl squad. Journalists should refrain from telling Hollywood how to remake the classics. But they know Hollywood is woke enough to take them seriously."

articles.title: Arturo Pérez-Reverte y sus declaraciones virales sobre Pedro Sánchez en 'El Hormiguero': "Es el político más interesante de España y probablemente de Europa"
articles.standfirst: Arturo Pérez-Reverte vuelve este miércoles, 18 de noviembre, a 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: Arturo Pérez-Reverte vuelve este miércoles, 18 de noviembre, a 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: El escritor y académico, Arturo Pérez-Reverte, será entrevistado por Pablo Motos para presentar su nueva novela, 'La hipótesis más peligrosa', en una semana especialmente marcada por la actualidad política. España afronta la recta final de la campaña electoral de las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre y la presencia del autor en el programa de Antena 3 vuelve a poner sobre la mesa una de las cuestiones que más comentarios han generado en sus anteriores visitas: sus opiniones sobre los políticos españoles y, especialmente, sobre Pedro Sánchez. No sería la primera vez que Pérez-Reverte deja titulares sobre el presidente del Gobierno en el plató de Pablo Motos. En noviembre de 2023, durante una entrevista en la que también habló de la ley de amnistía y de la situación política del país, el escritor realizó un retrato muy particular del líder socialista. Unas declaraciones que se han recuperado en numerosas ocasiones desde entonces y que el propio autor volvió a compartir en sus redes sociales en junio de 2025. "Es un pistolero, un asesino, un tipo que no repara en nada", afirmó entonces al referirse a Sánchez. Pérez-Reverte matizó que no estaba haciendo una valoración moral convencional, sino analizando al presidente desde la perspectiva de un novelista y de alguien interesado en los mecanismos del poder. En aquella entrevista, emitida en noviembre de 2023, Pablo Motos preguntó al escritor por Pedro Sánchez y por su capacidad para mantenerse al frente del Gobierno. Pérez-Reverte reconoció que el presidente le parecía un personaje fascinante desde el punto de vista político, aunque dejó claro que esa consideración no significaba compartir sus decisiones ni su ideología. "Es un aventurero de la política", explicó antes de añadir que tenía "ese instinto asesino del jugador de ajedrez". También destacó su habilidad para manejar los tiempos y las circunstancias políticas: "Tiene un instinto político extraordinario. Es valiente, tenaz, atrevido, no tiene escrúpulos ninguno. Es el político más interesante de España y probablemente de Europa". El escritor llegó a compararlo con un personaje de ficción: "En una novela lo pondría de malo maquiavélico". Y resumió su impresión con una frase que también tuvo mucho recorrido: "El aplomo, el descaro, el cinismo... Es que no hay un tío como él. Soy un fan suyo". Aquella no fue su última reflexión sobre el presidente en el programa de Antena 3. El 4 de noviembre de 2024, cuando acudió para presentar 'La isla de la mujer dormida', Pablo Motos volvió a preguntarle por el dirigente socialista. En esa ocasión, Pérez-Reverte lo definió como un político con una combinación de cualidades que, a su juicio, lo convertían en un personaje excepcional. "Su desvergüenza política, su cinismo, su ambición, su deseo de aferrarse en el poder a toda costa y su falta de escrúpulos le convierten en un personaje único", afirmó. También recurrió a una metáfora para explicar su estrategia: "Es una partida de póker y nos está desplumando". En septiembre de 2025, el escritor regresó a 'El Hormiguero' y volvió a hablar de Sánchez, aunque reconoció que ya no le despertaba la misma fascinación: "Ya no me fascina, ahora quiero estudiar a otro, pero no se va a ir, ¿dónde va a ir?", comentó. Este miércoles, Pérez-Reverte volverá a sentarse frente a Pablo Motos en un contexto político diferente, con la campaña electoral en su recta final y un debate entre los principales candidatos previsto para el jueves 19 de noviembre. Su entrevista tiene como motivo principal la presentación de su nueva novela, pero sus anteriores intervenciones demuestran que la actualidad política suele acabar ocupando una parte importante de la conversación. Queda por ver si esta vez vuelve a dejar alguna declaración sobre los dirigentes que protagonizan la campaña.
